# Load the dataset from the correct path
DATA_PATH = 'data/dataset.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Display the first few rows of the dataframe
df.head()

# Check the column names and data types in the dataframe
df.info()  # This will provide information about the columns and their data types

# Fill missing values in the temperature column with the mean temperature
df['temperature_C'].fillna(df['temperature_C'].mean(), inplace=True)

# Convert the measurement_date column to datetime format
df['measurement_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['measurement_date'])

# Verify the changes
df.info()  # Check the info again to confirm changes

# Extract the relevant columns for analysis
temperature_data = df[['measurement_date', 'temperature_C']]

# Set the measurement_date as the index for easier time series analysis
temperature_data.set_index('measurement_date', inplace=True)

# Display the first few rows of the prepared data
temperature_data.head()

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define the sinusoidal model function
def sinusoidal_model(t, A, B, C, D):
    return A * np.sin(B * t + C) + D

# Prepare the time variable (in days)
temperature_data['time'] = (temperature_data.index - temperature_data.index[0]).days

# Fit the sinusoidal model to the data
popt, pcov = curve_fit(sinusoidal_model, temperature_data['time'], temperature_data['temperature_C'], 
                       p0=[10, 2 * np.pi / 365, 0, 0])  # Initial guess for parameters

# Extract the fitted parameters
A, B, C, D = popt

# Calculate the fitted values
fitted_values = sinusoidal_model(temperature_data['time'], A, B, C, D)

# Plot the original data and the fitted curve
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(temperature_data.index, temperature_data['temperature_C'], label='Observed Temperature', color='blue')
plt.plot(temperature_data.index, fitted_values, label='Fitted Sinusoidal Model', color='red')
plt.title('Temperature Data and Fitted Sinusoidal Model')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Temperature (°C)')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

# Display the estimated parameters
A, B, C, D

# Calculate R-squared value
residuals = temperature_data['temperature_C'] - fitted_values
ss_res = np.sum(residuals**2)
ss_tot = np.sum((temperature_data['temperature_C'] - np.mean(temperature_data['temperature_C']))**2)
r_squared = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

# Display the R-squared value
r_squared
